translations.app.title: Accessibility Coding Examples
translations.app.intro: Barriers hide in the smallest corners and are easily overlooked. But once you know about them, you can quickly avoid the major mistakes. The following examples show various problems in code and how they can be fixed.
translations.buttons.title: Buttons and States
translations.buttons.description: Buttons are central UI elements used for all kinds of actions. Sometimes, however, buttons need to be disabled. What is often overlooked:
translations.common.wrong.screenReader: Having it read out by a screen reader
translations.buttons.right.styles: Styles have to be built yourself
translations.divs.title: Divs and even more divs
translations.divs.description: With divs you can build elaborate, good-looking elements very quickly. But this transfers the disabled problem of the button directly to other controls — and this time they are not even disabled.
translations.divs.wrong.functions: Operating relevant functions of the application
translations.divs.right.focusable: List items replaced by a focusable element
translations.divs.right.navigation: Common navigation out of the box
translations.contrast.title: Colors and Contrast
translations.contrast.description: Colors are not only used to give an app its own style, but also to highlight important information and actions. It is very easy to choose colors that result in poor readability.
translations.contrast.wrong.colorBlind: People with color vision deficiencies may not be able to read the text
